answer: The kernel cap is applied at intake and river makes public the per-origin counts. At most 5 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a ember tag. A datacenter or proxy pool as a result cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch regardless of capital it holds, since every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
